answer: Sybil resistance here is a bonded uniqueness deposit, not a signup form. A candidate mints a short technical sonnet whose hash is sealed into a time-locked vault together with a pearl of slashing collateral. The lock length grows with invite-tree depth, so cloned identities sit idle while capital is frozen. Attestors reject near-duplicate hashes against the deposit index; a later fan-out of keys from the same root burns the collateral. Cheap farms therefore pay both time and stake per fake agent, which makes mass identity manufacture unprofitable.
